networkRef.description: The network's reference for this demand.

siteId.description: The fulfillment site the demand is destined for.

state.description: `NEW` is received and unanswered, with the clock running. `SUBMITTED` means we answered and told the network, but that submission has not yet been reconciled against the network's own transaction-status record (a 200 on the submit call is accepted-for-processing, never itself a settled commitment). `ACKNOWLEDGED` is a settled commitment to fulfil in full, reached once reconciliation confirms it — the protocol has no partial acknowledgement. `REJECTED` is a refusal, and just as valid an answer: a deadline we cannot meet, or a submission the network itself refused, is better refused than missed. `CONFIRMED` means shipment has been confirmed to the network.

requiredShipBy.description: The deadline the NETWORK set. This context did not choose it and cannot move it.

acknowledgeBy.description: When our answer is due — 24 hours after the demand ARRIVED, matching the counterparty's published SLA. Anchored to arrival and then stored, never recomputed: a batch that arrives after an outage may already be near or past its window, and recomputing would silently reset every one of those clocks.

localOrderId.description: The order raised in order-management for this demand. Absent until acknowledged, because local work must never exist for demand we have not committed to. An explicitly stored mapping, never derived from a string convention.

acknowledgementOverdue.description: Whether the window has closed with this order still unanswered. Derived using the same domain rule the sweep enforces, so this surface cannot disagree with the sweep about what overdue means.

networkLineRef.description: The network's identity for this line, unique only WITHIN its order rather than globally.

networkProductId.description: The network's product identifier (an ASIN, in the counterparty's vocabulary). Not a SKU.

sku.description: Our product identity, resolved from `networkProductId` by this context's translation dictionary. Demand naming a product we cannot translate is rejected in full, because we cannot acknowledge in full what we cannot identify in full.

500.description: An RFC 7807 problem document. A NUL character (U+0000) is never valid input (PostgreSQL text cannot hold it): in the request path it is a 404 `resource-not-found`, in a query parameter a 400 `invalid-request`, and in a request body a 400 `malformed-request-body`.
